identity.real_world_identity_notes: Aston Martin identifies the 2024 Vantage GT3 as a comprehensive evolution sharing the mechanical architecture of the previous Vantage GT3/GTE. The predecessor's six-speed sequential hardware and the exact AMS2 paddle interface are kept distinct in provenance.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim without an integrated display or wheel-mounted shift lights.

notes: The car moved from rest without physical clutch input; the underlying simulator mechanism was not established.
All six paddle gears accepted clutchless full-throttle upshifts with automatic cut and clutchless downshifts with automatic blip.
Guided live test completed with Auto Clutch and Auto Shifting disabled.
Clutch-free move-off, six paddle gears, automatic cut/blip, and the closed no-display rim were directly observed.

confidence.basis: Exact identity and complete user-facing AMS2 control behavior were directly tested; Aston Martin lineage sources independently support the six-speed sequential architecture.

claims.basis: Official release/manufacturer sources and exact live telemetry establish the model and simulator identity.
Aston Martin establishes shared predecessor architecture and the predecessor's six-speed sequential hardware; exact paddle actuation and six gears were exercised in AMS2.
Guided current-game testing directly established move-off, automatic cut/blip, actuation, and wheel details.

notes: The simulator mechanism permitting clutch-free move-off remains explicitly unknown.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Paddle sequential that asks for no clutch at any point: it gets away from rest, cuts the upshift and blips the downshift itself. Once you are in the car the gearbox is not your problem.
